name: gaze
measures: Scenario 3, gaze jumping (Quad Views' upstream debug_simulate_tracking=1 in the COPIED settings.cfg: the gaze is the OS cursor, tangent t -> desktop x = 500 + 350 t). Quad Views log: 'DCSVR gaze: ... saccades' > 0, about 2 per 1.4 s, widened > 0. Capture around each jump: focus field of view of the real frame after the jump moved by the commanded tangent (+ lead); synthetic focus field of view == the next real frame's; synthetic alpha == the next frame's; the zone the previous frame did not cover: not black where alpha > 0, layer mismatch <= 2 x the interior's. Flight log: foveated_mode result=1 and no result=2. Arm fill1 = foveated_uncovered_fill=1 as the second remedy.
cannotJudge: Visibility of the fill during a real saccade (saccadic suppression); real saccade dynamics (the cursor is stepped in 3 moves 10 ms apart, harsher than an eye); the real tracker's latency and noise. Sign and scale of the cursor-to-gaze mapping are read in the code only: the first run draws Quad Views' gaze marker (debug_eye_gaze=1, a 20 px square) into the submitted image; look at compose.py's picture.
sideEffects: debug_simulate_tracking calls ClipCursor(1,1,999,999) on every located frame, from the briefing on: the mouse is confined to the top-left 1000 x 1000 px of the desktop while DCS runs. The runner moves DCS's window to the desktop origin before the FLY click and calls ClipCursor(NULL) after DCS has closed
gaze and DCS's mouse cursor are the same device: the cockpit cursor moves with every jump; smooth_cursor=0 in the copied ofxr_bridge.ini so OFXR's cursor path stays out of this scenario
everything fed by Quad Views' gaze export follows the simulated gaze (eye-focus blur, G vision, fixation depth, Depth boost)
90 submissions per capture = about 1 s at 90 Hz, so each window holds one or two jumps; scale 2 keeps it at 0.9 GB per capture
